value.title: The Measure of Mercy
value.premise: A bridge toll and a bell that rings thirteen times lead from local corruption to royal succession, transcontinental archives, and the old responsibility of a dragon—without losing sight of supper, friendship, weather, work, and ordinary lives worth protecting.
partyGoals: Become part of Bramblebridge without taking over its life.
Learn who profits from the new toll orders and why an empty tax wagon reached the market.
Choose how powerful systems can be made humane without making every victory belong to one conspiracy.
toneAndBoundaries: Cozy, lightly humorous, storybook medieval adventure grounded in believable work, law, travel, weather, and consequence.
Magic is rare and remarkable rather than ordinary infrastructure; grief and danger appear beside warmth, eccentricity, and recovery.
Mysteries reward secrets, riddles, conversation, and creative solutions; apparent bosses may reveal higher layers while completed adventures still matter.

entities.name: A Cat With Its Own Will

value.summary: Ganji has a natural affinity for cats. A planned future story hook: he may cross paths with a cat of unusual, independent will that can understand him -- a possible companion, given his affinity, playable as a small optional thread rather than a major plot point.
value.provenance: GM worldbuilding note, from player-provided character background

value.summary: An elven sect-brother felt it improper that Ganji didn't speak Elvish, and privately taught him the language during free hours.
Two weeks ago, Ganji left the Tensor Sect in the dark of night and has been travelling the Lantern Road toward Bramblebridge since.

An old traveling musician once stayed at the Tensor Sect for a short time. Music wasn't permitted within the Sect's walls, so he played just outside them instead -- where Ganji, sneaking out from his required hours of solitary religious study, heard him. The two struck a quiet bargain not to tell on each other, became friends over the musician's short stay, and Ganji learned to play the flute from him. It was Ganji's first real experience of music, and part of why he later carved his quarterstaff to double as one.
The Tensor Sect named Ganji 'the Unbidden Eye,' believing his birth fulfilled an old teaching about a student who sees before learning how to look.
value.provenance: Tensor Sect internal teaching, known to Ganji and sect members

value.summary: Set into the base of one of Bramblebridge's bridge piers is a small stone alcove, sealed by a door bearing a faded royal crest nobody currently living can place. Since the new toll order arrived, guards have been quietly posted to keep people away from it -- and get oddly tense if asked why.
value.provenance: Observable in Bramblebridge; the guards' behavior is common gossip

value.summary: The season's royal tax wagon arrived at Bramblebridge's market completely empty -- seals unbroken, locks untouched, no sign of a break-in anywhere along the road. The crown's collectors are furious and looking for someone local to blame before word reaches the capital.

Thistlewick's shepherds have lost eleven sheep this month -- no blood, no tracks, no wolves seen or heard. Each one vanished at night, always from the pastures nearest Sable Hollow. The villagers are more baffled than afraid, but they'd very much like it to stop.
value.provenance: Local rumor, easily heard in Bramblebridge or Thistlewick

value.summary: Sect doctrine holds that nobody can cross the Prediction Court's suspended bells without ringing one — until Ganji did it on the night he escaped.
value.provenance: Tensor Sect legend, now spreading among the monks

value.summary: The Tensor Sect teaches that every movement is joined to every other by invisible tension, and that a sufficiently disciplined mind could perceive the whole pattern at once.
value.provenance: Tensor Sect teaching, widely known within Highmead

value.summary: The Tensor Sect raised Ganji as a prodigy and does not easily let go of what it considers its own. If Ganji ever makes a serious, lasting break from them, the Sect may dispatch monks to retrieve him. This is a live, unresolved threat for the GM to invoke at a dramatically appropriate moment, not a scheduled event.
value.provenance: GM worldbuilding note, from player-provided character background

value.summary: A small, quiet wood at the edge of Thistlewick's pastures. Nothing dangerous has ever come out of it -- but lately things have been going into it and not coming back.

A small shepherd village half a day up the Lantern Road from Bramblebridge, known for its wool and for the ring of old standing stones on the hill above the pastures. Quiet, insular, and currently missing sheep.
A country of pale hills and old chalk pits, threaded by the Lantern Road between the hill-city of Highmead and the frontier village of Bramblebridge.

Ganji's catlike traits have no confirmed cause -- mutation, old curse, or something dormant in the buried past of the region. Several pages about his family were deliberately removed from the Tensor Sect's own records, and even the Sect doesn't fully understand why. Ganji himself assumes his birth parents abandoned him simply because of how he looked, and isn't especially curious to learn otherwise -- but the truth (if the GM chooses to reveal one) has never been told to him.
The pages removed from Ganji's childhood record have resurfaced among documents pulled from a Button Hills sinkhole — proof the sect knew more about his ancestry than it admitted.

The alcove holds an old binding ward tied to a pact struck generations ago with a dragon that once guarded this river crossing before any bridge existed. The ward is failing, slowly. The new toll order exists because someone in the crown found out and wants the site quietly monitored without causing public panic ahead of the succession. This is a slow-burn campaign-arc thread, not meant to resolve in one session -- no fixed reward or XP yet; the GM should let its shape emerge through play rather than solving it early.

The wagon has a false bottom, cut and reset by a Bramblebridge cartwright who owed a debt to a moneylender. Somewhere along the route the real silver was swapped for lead-weighted sacks and offloaded at a covered mill outside town; the seals were never broken because the swap happened before the wagon was sealed for the day. Expected solution path: examine the wagon's underside (Investigation), trace the route and timing (Insight/Investigation with witnesses), confront or catch the cartwright. Reward: 30 gp finder's fee plus real goodwill with the tollhouse if the silver is recovered; 75 XP for solving it, more if handled with unexpected cleverness or mercy.

A fey-touched cat with a will of its own has been quietly herding sheep into a hidden glen in Sable Hollow, keeping them as its own odd little kingdom -- not malicious, just lonely and mischievous. It can understand speech even if it doesn't answer. Expected solution path: track it (Survival/Perception), follow it into the Hollow, and either negotiate, play, or simply be kind to it rather than fight -- violence toward it should feel wrong and unnecessary once found. This cat may be the same one hinted at in Ganji's cat-companion hook; GM discretion on making the connection explicit. Reward: the shepherds' genuine gratitude, 20 gp, a wheel of cheese, and 50 XP; a possible ongoing feline companion if Ganji makes friends with it.

No one helped Ganji cross the Prediction Court unheard — it was entirely his own perception. But at least one monk suspects otherwise, and privately wonders if they should have helped him leave sooner.

value.summary: A character sheet gathers the character's available identity, abilities, defenses, features, resources, actions, and equipment into one readable view.

blocks.heading: Available state

blocks.heading: Authority

value.title: Weapon Attacks
value.summary: A weapon attack resolves its attack roll and, on a hit, applies the weapon activity's recorded damage through the active combat mechanics.

blocks.heading: Resolution
items: Choose the acting character, target, and recorded weapon activity.
Resolve the attack roll against the target's current defense.
If the attack hits, resolve the activity's damage and the target's recorded damage responses.

blocks.heading: Recorded state wins
blocks.body: The readable rule never substitutes browser calculations for the active weapon-attack mechanic.

examples.title: Different weapon activities
examples.body: A weapon definition can expose distinct melee, thrown, one-handed, or two-handed activities. The selected activity determines the authoritative mechanic input.

value.title: Long Rests
value.summary: A long rest is a recorded episode whose progress, interruptions, completion benefits, and eligible resource restoration are resolved by the active rest policy.

blocks.heading: Rest episode
blocks.body: Beginning a rest records the selected policy and starting state. Progress and interruptions update that same episode rather than inventing an outcome in the interface.

blocks.heading: What the mechanic checks
items: The active rest policy and its source-bound timing.
Hit points, Hit Dice, exhaustion, ability scores, and resource pools that are eligible for restoration when the episode completes.

examples.title: Interrupted rest
examples.body: When an interruption is recorded, the rest-progress mechanic applies the active policy before reporting whether more time is required.

value.appearance: A half-elf, son of a human father and an elven mother he never knew. Ganji mostly looks the part -- until you notice the eyes, faintly catlike and quick to catch light, or the too-smooth, unnervingly graceful way he moves, like a cat crossing a fence rail. It can be a little offputting to people who aren't used to it. He's eighteen, technically grown by most reckonings, though he rarely acts it.
value.biography:
Ganji was born in a small rural village and abandoned as an infant -- by his own reckoning, over nothing more than how he looked. Word of the odd, unnervingly graceful baby spread by rumor, and within months travelers came to investigate, convinced he might be something prophesied. The Tensor Sect took him in.

The Sect believes that mastering combat through perfect perception and prediction is the path to one day "seeing god," and they raised Ganji as a prodigy of natural gifts -- inhumanly nimble, unnervingly perceptive -- while holding him to punishing standards for a devotion he never quite felt. He trained personally under the Sect's Headmaster, its strongest warrior, and made what friends he could. But there were no women among the Sect's ranks, and that was only one of many things that wore at him over the years.

He was meant to spend his required hours of solitude on religious study, but he often slipped away instead. It was on one of those escapes that he heard an old traveling musician -- forbidden from playing inside the Sect's walls -- practicing just outside them. The two struck a quiet bargain not to tell on each other, became friends over the musician's short stay, and Ganji learned to play the flute from him: his first real taste of something that wasn't devotion, discipline, or god. The Sect, for its part, once gave him a carving knife as a gift, a mark of how important they believed him to be -- an enchanted blade that never dulls and can shave stone like wood, though no one ever explained where its magic came from. Ganji used it to carve himself a quarterstaff, hollowed and fingerholed to double as a flute -- since he was meant to be training combat, not music, a 'weapon' that was secretly an instrument let him practice openly without ever needing to hide it.

Two weeks ago, tired of chasing a faith that never took root in him, Ganji slipped away from the Sect's halls in the dark of night. He's been on the road since, only now starting to slow down -- half-expecting that if he ever truly tries to leave for good, the Sect will send monks after him.

He doesn't spend much time wondering why he is the way he is. He'd rather find out who he's going to be. He fights because he's always been good at it and likes winning; he wants adventure, good company, maybe someone to fall for, and above all a reason to care about something the way his sect-brothers cared for their god.
value.playerNotes: Fighting style: prefers fists and feet, but is just as happy with a weapon in hand -- especially the quarterstaff he carved himself, which doubles as a flute -- or whatever else is nearby. When he loses or embarrasses himself, he laughs it off and tries something reckless rather than sulking; laid-back, easygoing, almost Taoist in temperament. Traveling alone. Looking for fun, adventure, friendship, and maybe romance eventually, more than any grand destiny. Player is fine with character death and would enjoy Ganji's story surfacing as lore in a future campaign set in this world.
